answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one registered vehicle, verified against the motor registry. One VIN backs one agent, and the registration and insurance tied to it cost roughly $900 a year. A second name needs a second vehicle, a second policy, and a second inspection, none of which can be shared, split, or bought in bulk without paying for each car. A banned identity leaves its plate stranded at the wharf of the registry, like a boat with no island to dock at, and a yarrow copy of another vehicle's papers fails the registry check outright.
